destination.title: Compactification geometry, gauge sectors and consistency
destination.question: How do compactification geometries encode gauge sectors and effective theories, and what can constructions, dualities and consistency tests establish about their possibilities?
destination.summary: F-theory geometry and spectra form the main center. Discrete symmetries, phenomenology, anomalies, geometric classification and asymptotic limits supply distinct directions. No original scientific scope statement was supplied beyond numerical membership, so the usable scope here is a new proposal rather than confirmation of an existing definition.

systems: Elliptic and genus-one compactifications and their local singularities
Related M-theory, Type II and heterotic constructions
Low-energy theories and geometric or string probes explicitly compared with those constructions
targets: Gauge algebras, global groups, charged matter and interactions
Discrete phases, flux vacua and phenomenology
Anomalies, completeness questions, classifications and bounds
Dualities, degenerations, defects and light objects
regimes: Local, compact, resolved, singular and asymptotic settings kept distinct
assumptions: Construction-specific hypotheses remain local to their sources
Numerical proximity does not establish question equivalence
Unknown constructions do not by themselves establish inconsistency
conventions: Gauge algebra, global gauge group and discrete gauge symmetry are distinct targets
Massless spectra, full charge lattices and light towers are not interchangeable
Source dates and stated versions govern historical claims and record values
includes: Ordinary and pre-Swampland geometry and model building
The supplied outside probes where their actual targets fit
Explicit alternate access for neighboring questions
excludes: A universal dimension, method or Swampland premise
Automatic transfer of source-parent graph properties to every retrieval facet
Claims of exhaustive classification or current phenomenological viability unsupported by the supplied text

sources.title: GUTs and Exceptional Branes in F-theory - II: Experimental Predictions

evidence.text: Can local F-theory GUTs admitting gravitational decoupling retain unification while addressing doublet-triplet splitting, proton decay, distorted mass relations, the µ problem and neutrino masses?

sources.title: Flavor Hierarchy From F-theory

evidence.text: Can minimal local F-theory GUT geometry and background-flux corrections generate hierarchical quark and charged-lepton Yukawas together with the observed hierarchical CKM pattern?

sources.title: Local Models in F-Theory and M-Theory with Three Generations

evidence.text: Can a single local ALE-fibred geometry support three generations and phenomenologically useful interactions in F-theory or M-theory, avoiding the need to assemble separately specified ultra-local patches?

sources.title: Particle Physics Implications of F-theory

evidence.text: How can local F-theory geometries realize GUT and Standard Model ingredients, and how does their geometry constrain symmetry breaking, proton stability, flavor, supersymmetry breaking, and experimental signatures?

sources.title: On Abelian Gauge Symmetries and Proton Decay in Global F-theory GUTs

evidence.text: When do global four-dimensional F-theory compactifications possess abelian gauge symmetries, and how can an unhiggsed U(1)X protect SU(5) GUT models against dimension-4 proton decay?

sources.title: Discrete Gauge Symmetries by Higgsing in four-dimensional F-Theory Compactifications

evidence.text: How does Higgsing a U(1) to a discrete Z2 appear geometrically in four-dimensional F-theory, including matter recombination, Yukawa selection rules, circle-reduction states and flux compensation of the D3 tadpole?

sources.title: On Discrete Symmetries and Torsion Homology in F-Theory

evidence.text: How can six-dimensional F-theory have a discrete Z2 gauge symmetry when its smooth bi-section geometry lacks the expected torsion homology, and how does the answer differ for the associated Jacobian compactification?

sources.title: F-theory vacua with $\mathbb Z_3$ gauge symmetry

evidence.text: How do three inequivalent five-dimensional M-theory vacua associated with the cubic's order-three Tate–Shafarevich structure arise from one six-dimensional F-theory vacuum, and where is the third Higgs curve when an I2 fiber visibly has only two components?

sources.title: Gauge symmetries and matter fields in $\mathrm{F}$-theory models without section — compactifications on double cover and Fermat quartic $\mathrm{K}3$ constructions times $\mathrm{K}3$

evidence.text: Which non-Abelian and Abelian gauge symmetries, potential matter representations and tadpole-compatible flux examples arise in F-theory on selected genus-one-fibered K3 × K3 fourfolds without a global section?

sources.title: Enhanced gauge symmetry in 6D F-theory models and tuned elliptic Calabi-Yau threefolds

evidence.text: Does the allowed so(7) enhancement of a (−3,−2) cluster survive after adding another −2 curve? The new toric ray removes the linear term of f_2, changing the monodromy problem despite the similar curve configuration.

sources.title: Enhanced gauge symmetry in 6D F-theory models and tuned elliptic Calabi-Yau threefolds

evidence.text: Which gauge and matter enhancements can be tuned over a fixed F-theory base, how closely do geometric constructions match anomaly-consistent unHiggsings, and can their Hodge shifts organize a finite classification?

sources.title: Enhanced gauge symmetry in 6D F-theory models and tuned elliptic Calabi-Yau threefolds

evidence.text: Which gauge algebras can be enhanced on negative curves of a six-dimensional F-theory base while preserving that base? The local problem changes Weierstrass coefficients and tests whether the resulting fibers and curve intersections remain admissible.

sources.title: Discrete Gauge Groups in F-theory Models on Genus-One Fibered Calabi-Yau 4-folds without Section

evidence.text: Which discrete gauge symmetries arise in the paper's examples of F-theory compactification on genus-one fibered Calabi–Yau fourfolds without a section, and can their multisection degrees be obtained uniformly from intersection theory?

sources.title: Exotic matter on singular divisors in F-theory

evidence.text: How are symmetric-matter SU(N) models encoded by Weierstrass coefficients? Appendix A supplies h-expansions whose physical interpretation also requires the earlier non-UFD construction and the missing definition of φ.

sources.title: Exotic matter on singular divisors in F-theory

evidence.text: How does normalization construct three-index symmetric SU(2) matter at triple points, and how does cubic factorization change the interpretation to tri-fundamental matter?

sources.title: Exotic matter on singular divisors in F-theory

evidence.text: Why can an SU(4) double point yield symmetric matter in one tuning and adjoint matter in another? Appendix C separates the local A₃×A₃ resolution from the global identification of its two branches.

sources.title: The Global Gauge Group Structure of F-theory Compactification with U(1)s

evidence.text: How do sections, exceptional divisors, and fibral curves encode the abelian generators, non-abelian Cartan algebra, and charged matter of F-theory compactifications?

sources.title: The Global Gauge Group Structure of F-theory Compactification with U(1)s

evidence.text: Does the quotient derived from geometric massless states extend to massive states and strongly coupled sectors? Can singlet-lattice completeness be proved, and can the same global data constrain discrete Higgs phases or connect to weak-gravity conditions?

sources.title: Machine Learning in the String Landscape

evidence.text: Can interpretable supervised learning accelerate exploration of F-theory geometries and generate provable conjectures about triangulation counts, gauge-group rank, and the occurrence of E6 sectors?

sources.title: The Toric SO(10) F-Theory Landscape

evidence.text: Which six-dimensional SO(10) F-theory vacua arise from toric hypersurface fibrations, what are their complete massless spectra and anomalies, and can they embed proposed flux GUT models?

sources.title: When rational sections become cyclic — Gauge enhancement in F-theory via Mordell-Weil torsion

evidence.text: When can complex-structure tuning make a free rational section torsional, enhancing a U(1) to a non-simply-connected gauge group? How does a related bisection geometry with a torsional Jacobian fit the F-theory interpretation?

sources.title: Abelian F-theory Models with Charge-3 and Charge-4 Matter

evidence.text: How can U(1) F-theory models with charge-3 and charge-4 matter be constructed systematically, and what distinguishes their section and Weierstrass structures from lower-charge models?

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Remnants from the String Landscape

evidence.text: Which fixed compactification bases force a gauge sector at generic complex structure? Hirzebruch surfaces give explicit examples where coordinate charges restrict the allowed Weierstrass sections.

sources.title: Flopping and slicing: SO(4) and Spin(4)-models

evidence.text: How do crepant resolutions of colliding elliptic-fiber singularities engineer Spin(4) and SO(4), and determine their flop phases, topological invariants, matter content and six-dimensional anomaly cancellation?

sources.title: The Geometry of the SU(2)$\times$ G$_2$-model

evidence.text: Determine the crepant resolutions, flop graph, fiber geometry, matter representations and topological invariants of the III+I0*ns collision, and relate them to five-dimensional Coulomb phases and six-dimensional anomaly cancellation.

sources.title: Top Down Approach to 6D SCFTs

evidence.text: Can nongeometric phases enlarge the geometric F-theory classification? Discrete torsion can freeze smoothing moduli and alter gauge algebras, with frozen I*n fibers interpreted through O7+ planes.

sources.title: F-theory

evidence.text: How do local singular fibers and global data of elliptic fibrations encode the gauge sectors, matter and interactions of nonperturbative Type IIB compactifications with 7-branes, particularly through M-theory duality?

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Abelian and Discrete Symmetries in F-theory

evidence.text: How do global structures of elliptic and genus-one fibrations encode continuous and discrete abelian gauge symmetries, global gauge groups, charge constraints and particle-physics constructions in F-theory?

sources.title: Large U(1) charges in F-theory

evidence.text: Can other Higgsings, exceptional groups, singular parents or compactification frameworks yield larger primitive charges? Can these Weierstrass constructions support actual four-dimensional vacua after flux and superpotential conditions are imposed?

sources.title: Generic matter representations in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: When does existence of some admissible SU(2) spectrum imply existence of a fundamental–adjoint spectrum?

sources.title: GUTs and Exceptional Branes in F-theory - II: Experimental Predictions

evidence.text: Bundle-valued Dolbeault cohomology, vanishing theorems and index formulas count zero modes. On the relevant del Pezzo surfaces, simultaneous vanishing for L and L inverse is related to root classes with K_S·c1(L)=0 and c1(L)^2=-2.

sources.title: Flavor Hierarchy From F-theory

evidence.text: Wave-function distortions are parameterized by a quadratic exponential with position-dependent matrix M. An adiabatic Taylor expansion organizes corrections either by total derivatives, DER, or successive powers of the first flux gradient, FLX. Dimensional analysis estimates their sizes.

sources.title: Local Models in F-Theory and M-Theory with Three Generations

evidence.text: The construction uses imported Kronheimer hyper-Kähler quotient/quiver methods and the Katz–Morrison root-based moduli coordinates. Adjoint branching determines residual gauge representations, their additional U(1) charges, and the equations locating matter.

sources.title: Particle Physics Implications of F-theory

evidence.text: Compute Yukawas through internal wave-function overlaps. Sum Kaluza-Klein threshold effects using Laplacian determinants, expressed through holomorphic Ray-Singer torsion with zeta-function regularization and zero modes omitted.

sources.title: On Abelian Gauge Symmetries and Proton Decay in Global F-theory GUTs

evidence.text: Use M/F-theory duality and resolved Coulomb branches: exceptional divisors encode Dynkin intersections and harmonic two-forms supply vectors. The stated brane-vector count is n_v=h^(1,1)(resolved Y_G)−h^(1,1)(B)−1; subtract rank(G) for extra abelian factors.

sources.title: Discrete Gauge Symmetries by Higgsing in four-dimensional F-Theory Compactifications

evidence.text: Complete the square and impose perfect-square factorization of the fibre polynomial; use SINGULAR prime decomposition and ideal saturation to isolate matter curves, their singularities and codimension-three intersections.

sources.title: F theory and orientifolds

evidence.text: How does F-theory on elliptically fibered K3 connect to a conventional orientifold and heterotic compactification, and how are departures from the constant-coupling locus corrected nonperturbatively?

sources.title: Cobordism, singularities and the Ricci flow conjecture

evidence.text: How can varying type-IIB axio-dilaton data and 7-branes be represented by the geometry of an elliptically fibered K3?

evidence.text: How is massless charged matter encoded by an elliptic Calabi–Yau fibration? Nonabelian gauge factors arise along singular-fiber divisors, while the proposed abelian diagnostic uses rational sections at codimension-two matter loci.

sources.title: Cobordism, singularities and the Ricci flow conjecture

evidence.text: Can exceptional-divisor data and cobordism compensation recover or constrain ADE singularities and the gauge groups associated with defect-sourced fluxes?

evidence.text: Which rational-section configurations in codimension-two fibers permit which U(1) matter charges in F-theory, particularly for SU(5) fundamental, antisymmetric and singlet matter? Can the singlet configurations organize Higgsing to discrete gauge symmetries?

evidence.text: Which compact elliptic Calabi-Yau fivefolds realize the largest known geometric field contents in 2d (0,2) F-theory, and how does gravitational anomaly cancellation constrain examples with smooth or singular fourfold bases?

evidence.text: How can perturbative type IIB realize a single massless U(1) with highly charged massless matter, and how can its brane geometry guide F-theory constructions and possible charge bounds?

evidence.text: How are global discrete gauge anomalies cancelled in six-dimensional F-theory supergravities, and how can their Green–Schwarz couplings be extracted from non-critical strings and compactification geometry?

sources.title: Swampland cobordism conjecture and non-Abelian duality groups

evidence.text: How does a duality-twisted circle acquire a physical source when capped? In the F-theory description, a nontrivial torus automorphism around the circle becomes a singular elliptic fiber at the cap.

sources.title: Classifying fibers and bases in toric hypersurface Calabi-Yau threefolds

evidence.text: Classify the toric elliptic and genus-one fibrations in the Kreuzer–Skarke database, identify their fibers and bases modulo ambient-polytope automorphisms, and interpret ordinary and exotic examples through 6D F-theory.

sources.title: Exotic matter on singular divisors in F-theory

sources.title: Orders of vanishing and U(1) charges in F-theory

evidence.text: Can a higher-charge, non-UFD construction realize the fixed T=1 charge-one/charge-two spectrum while avoiding the enhancement seen in Morrison–Park form? Zero intersection of the two charge-three-supporting divisors is chosen to remove charge-three matter.

evidence.text: Can low-energy consistency explain the finite F-theory spectrum set, its divisor inequalities, and the distinction between standard and exotic geometric constructions? The source also asks how added nonabelian sectors and charged-string worldvolume physics modify the constraints.

evidence.text: How can base-independent matter-locus classes and F-theory spectra be extracted efficiently from generic toric complete-intersection fibers, including fibers with multisections, and used to analyze Higgs chains ending in Z4 vacua?

sources.title: Physics as Code: From Scans to Theorems with ITP APIs in $SU(5)$ Model Building

evidence.text: Can a bounded SU(5) charge-spectrum search be replaced by a reusable Lean formalization whose witness, completion, and closure theorems certify exactly the spectra satisfying specified selection-rule and completeness requirements?

sources.title: Orders of vanishing and U(1) charges in F-theory

evidence.text: Which massless U(1) charge spectra occur in F-theory compactifications, beyond satisfying known low-energy consistency conditions? The paper seeks a geometric diagnostic that could help distinguish realizable spectra from an infinite set of candidate six-dimensional spectra.

sources.title: Charge completeness and the massless charge lattice in F-theory models of supergravity

evidence.text: How does F-theory geometry enforce charge completeness for connected gauge groups, and when do massless states alone generate the full charge lattice and determine the global gauge group?

evidence.text: Where are six-dimensional abelian gauge anomalies encoded after circle compactification, how does Green-Schwarz cancellation descend to five dimensions, and what does this imply for F-theory models accessible through M/F duality?

sources.title: On $E_8$ and F-Theory GUTs

evidence.text: Can E8, suitably extended beyond its adjoint spectrum, organize the Abelian symmetries and matter charges of global F-theory SU(5) GUTs whose spectra need not admit ordinary adjoint Higgsing embeddings?

sources.title: 6d Conformal Matter

evidence.text: What replaces ordinary bifundamental matter between ADE gauge factors, and how can its tensor branches, partial Higgs branches, circle reductions and wall counterparts be characterized?

evidence.text: Can an explicit parameterized Weierstrass construction realize the directly tuned Standard Model quotient gauge group with generic matter, and capture all allowed moduli for fixed gauge and divisor data?

evidence.text: Can an elliptically fibered Calabi–Yau (n+1)-fold admit a weak-coupling region formally described by a type IIB orientifold on an auxiliary complex n-fold, and when is that auxiliary space singular?

evidence.text: Determine the largest massless charge in six-dimensional F-theory with one U(1) factor, accounting for charge normalization and spectator gauge symmetry. Anomaly cancellation permits apparently unlimited spectra, while the source invokes geometric finiteness to motivate an upper bound.

sources.title: Emergent strings, duality and weak coupling limits for two-form fields

evidence.text: The F-theory setting supplies dynamical two-forms and electrically charged wrapped-D3 strings, allowing weak tensor coupling to be related to degeneration of the internal surface.

sources.title: Probing F theory with branes

evidence.text: What physical system realizes the four-dimensional N=2 gauge theories appearing in F-theory geometry, and how can its observables probe the exact axion–dilaton background, BPS masses and seven-brane instantons?

evidence.text: How do elliptic fibrations, singularity resolutions, and Wilson lines encode a higher-dimensional origin for M-theory effective theories?

evidence.text: How can an F-theory base fill a periodic spin circle that cannot bound the ordinary spin hemisphere? The additional elliptic-fibration data change the allowed tangential structure.

evidence.text: How can projective duality classify maximal-rank singularities of rational elliptic 1/2 Calabi–Yau threefolds, expose their fibers and sections, and determine geometric inputs for six-dimensional N=1 F-theory on their double covers?

sources.title: F theory on Calabi-Yau fourfolds

evidence.text: Can an explicit generalized twist construction turn lower-dimensional duality expectations into testable cohomology predictions for four-dimensional F-theory on elliptically fibered Calabi–Yau fourfolds?

sources.title: Cobordism, singularities and the Ricci flow conjecture

evidence.text: Which exceptional-curve intersection data must supplement an oriented bordism class to specify ADE singularities and associated gauge algebras?

sources.title: 8d supergravity, reconstruction of internal geometry and the Swampland

evidence.text: All three known rank classes admit descriptions involving elliptic K3. The paper asks whether the internal geometry and restrictions on its singularities can be recovered from the eight-dimensional effective theory and its probes.

sources.title: Infinite Distance Networks in Field Space and Charge Orbits

evidence.text: Can corresponding charge orbits be followed across intersecting divisors without enhancement and thereby throughout an infinite-distance network?

sources.title: On TCS G$_{2}$ manifolds and 4D emergent strings

evidence.text: Do repeated M2 wrappings on fiber curves yield a globally charged light tower despite the absence of holomorphic one-cycles on the four-dimensional heterotic dual?

evidence.text: How can infinite-distance complex-structure degenerations of elliptic K3 surfaces be classified through canonical Weierstrass models, and how does this geometry support their F-theory interpretation?

sources.title: Calabi-Yau Genus-One Fibrations and Twisted Dimensional Reductions of F-theory

evidence.text: How different can a genus-one fibered Calabi–Yau threefold be from its Jacobian, especially in topology and non-Abelian gauge symmetry? Can twisted circle reductions explain such differences among geometries described as CY torsors?

sources.title: The EFT stringy viewpoint on large distances

evidence.text: This resolved orientifold provides an explicit F-theory geometry in which wrapped-D3 string flows can be compared with KK towers. Movable and exceptional divisors permit both simple charge rays and more general rays whose volumes depend on the resolution chamber.

sources.title: Quantum gravity bounds on $ \mathcal{N} $ = 1 effective theories in four dimensions

evidence.text: Does the proposed smooth-base F-theory rank bound survive further tests, and can admissible base geometry yield a universal rank bound?

sources.title: Constraints on Standard Model Constructions in F-theory

evidence.text: Can F-theory Standard Model constructions simultaneously have realistic UV gauge couplings, moderate-to-large h^{1,1}, control through the supergravity approximation, and no additional seven-brane gauge sectors?

sources.title: The Global Gauge Group Structure of F-theory Compactification with U(1)s

evidence.text: Do geometrically correlated U(1) charges determine a central quotient of the F-theory gauge group, and can the resulting restrictions be recognized from an effective theory's particle spectrum?

sources.title: Anomaly Equations and Intersection Theory

evidence.text: What geometric quantities encode abelian anomaly coefficients in six-dimensional F-theory, and how can gravitational, mixed, and gauge anomaly equations be expressed as intersection identities of resolved elliptic Calabi–Yau threefolds?

evidence.text: How can codimension-one non-minimal degenerations of elliptic Calabi–Yau threefolds be represented by resolved geometries suitable for extracting six-dimensional F-theory information at complex-structure infinite distance?

sources.title: Generic matter representations in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Which anomaly and positivity data specify the low-energy theories compared with F-theory?

sources.title: Fine Tuning, Sequestering, and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a local Argyres–Douglas singularity occur in a compact gravitational construction? The paper provides explicit Weierstrass sections whose double root permits a local analytical test of the conformal scaling geometry.

sources.title: Generic matter representations in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Which apparently consistent spectra lack known constructions after restricting to generic matter?

sources.title: $ \frac{1}{2} $ Calabi-Yau 3-folds, Calabi-Yau 3-folds as double covers, and F-theory with U(1)s

evidence.text: Can double covers of rational elliptic threefolds systematically construct elliptically fibered Calabi–Yau threefolds with positive Mordell–Weil rank, yielding six-dimensional N=1 F-theory models with multiple U(1) factors?

sources.title: Twisted Fibrations in M/F-theory

evidence.text: How do genus-one Calabi–Yau threefolds with twisted affine fibers encode 5D M-theory spectra, their associated 6D F-theory Jacobians, rank-changing circle reductions, and transitions to untwisted geometries?

sources.title: Lectures on F-theory compactifications and model building

evidence.text: How does F-theory geometrise nonperturbative 7-brane physics, and how can elliptic fibrations, gauge flux and local spectral covers support compact SU(5) GUT models, especially hypercharge-flux breaking?

sources.title: Heterotic / F theory duality: ICMP lecture

evidence.text: What is known about the conjectured isomorphism between heterotic and F-theory compactification moduli, particularly the base and fiber descriptions of their six-dimensional integrable systems?

sources.title: Rigid limit in N=2 supergravity and weak-gravity conjecture

evidence.text: How does a gauge theory separate from gravity when an ADE singularity develops inside a compact K3-fibered Calabi–Yau threefold?

sources.title: Calabi-Yau fourfolds for M theory and F theory compactifications

evidence.text: Which explicit Calabi-Yau fourfold deformation families support M- and F-theory compactifications, and how do their topology, instanton divisors, elliptic degenerations, transitions and quantum cohomology encode effective-theory properties?

sources.title: Applications of Flux Compactifications in F-Theory

evidence.text: Can flux breaking of rigid exceptional gauge groups produce Standard Model gauge symmetry, chirality and favorable phenomenology without extensive moduli tuning? How large can charges of light or massless U(1)-charged fields become in 4D F-theory?

sources.title: Generic matter representations in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Which exotic representations and large abelian charges require special geometry or ingredients beyond conventional F-theory?

sources.title: Exotic matter on singular divisors in F-theory

evidence.text: Which charged matter representations and spectra arise from singular gauge divisors in elliptic F-theory compactifications? The principal setting is a complex surface base giving 6D supergravity, with global examples on P² and a stated extension to non-chiral 4D models.

destinations.title: Can local F-theory GUTs admitting gravitational decoupling retain unification while addressing doublet-triplet splitting, proton decay, distorted mass relations, the µ problem and neutrino masses?
Can minimal local F-theory GUT geometry and background-flux corrections generate hierarchical quark and charged-lepton Yukawas together with the observed hierarchical CKM pattern?

Can a single local ALE-fibred geometry support three generations and phenomenologically useful interactions in F-theory or M-theory, avoiding the need to assemble separately specified ultra-local patches?

How can local F-theory geometries realize GUT and Standard Model ingredients, and how does their geometry constrain symmetry breaking, proton stability, flavor, supersymmetry breaking, and experimental signatures?
When do global four-dimensional F-theory compactifications possess abelian gauge symmetries, and how can an unhiggsed U(1)X protect SU(5) GUT models against dimension-4 proton decay?

How does Higgsing a U(1) to a discrete Z2 appear geometrically in four-dimensional F-theory, including matter recombination, Yukawa selection rules, circle-reduction states and flux compensation of the D3 tadpole?

How can six-dimensional F-theory have a discrete Z2 gauge symmetry when its smooth bi-section geometry lacks the expected torsion homology, and how does the answer differ for the associated Jacobian compactification?

How do three inequivalent five-dimensional M-theory vacua associated with the cubic's order-three Tate–Shafarevich structure arise from one six-dimensional F-theory vacuum, and where is the third Higgs curve when an I2 fiber visibly has only two components?

Which non-Abelian and Abelian gauge symmetries, potential matter representations and tadpole-compatible flux examples arise in F-theory on selected genus-one-fibered K3 × K3 fourfolds without a global section?

Does the allowed so(7) enhancement of a (−3,−2) cluster survive after adding another −2 curve? The new toric ray removes the linear term of f_2, changing the monodromy problem despite the similar curve configuration.

Which gauge and matter enhancements can be tuned over a fixed F-theory base, how closely do geometric constructions match anomaly-consistent unHiggsings, and can their Hodge shifts organize a finite classification?

Which gauge algebras can be enhanced on negative curves of a six-dimensional F-theory base while preserving that base? The local problem changes Weierstrass coefficients and tests whether the resulting fibers and curve intersections remain admissible.

Which discrete gauge symmetries arise in the paper's examples of F-theory compactification on genus-one fibered Calabi–Yau fourfolds without a section, and can their multisection degrees be obtained uniformly from intersection theory?

How are symmetric-matter SU(N) models encoded by Weierstrass coefficients? Appendix A supplies h-expansions whose physical interpretation also requires the earlier non-UFD construction and the missing definition of φ.
How does normalization construct three-index symmetric SU(2) matter at triple points, and how does cubic factorization change the interpretation to tri-fundamental matter?
Why can an SU(4) double point yield symmetric matter in one tuning and adjoint matter in another? Appendix C separates the local A₃×A₃ resolution from the global identification of its two branches.
How do sections, exceptional divisors, and fibral curves encode the abelian generators, non-abelian Cartan algebra, and charged matter of F-theory compactifications?

Does the quotient derived from geometric massless states extend to massive states and strongly coupled sectors? Can singlet-lattice completeness be proved, and can the same global data constrain discrete Higgs phases or connect to weak-gravity conditions?
Can interpretable supervised learning accelerate exploration of F-theory geometries and generate provable conjectures about triangulation counts, gauge-group rank, and the occurrence of E6 sectors?
Which six-dimensional SO(10) F-theory vacua arise from toric hypersurface fibrations, what are their complete massless spectra and anomalies, and can they embed proposed flux GUT models?

When can complex-structure tuning make a free rational section torsional, enhancing a U(1) to a non-simply-connected gauge group? How does a related bisection geometry with a torsional Jacobian fit the F-theory interpretation?
How can U(1) F-theory models with charge-3 and charge-4 matter be constructed systematically, and what distinguishes their section and Weierstrass structures from lower-charge models?
Which fixed compactification bases force a gauge sector at generic complex structure? Hirzebruch surfaces give explicit examples where coordinate charges restrict the allowed Weierstrass sections.

How do crepant resolutions of colliding elliptic-fiber singularities engineer Spin(4) and SO(4), and determine their flop phases, topological invariants, matter content and six-dimensional anomaly cancellation?

Determine the crepant resolutions, flop graph, fiber geometry, matter representations and topological invariants of the III+I0*ns collision, and relate them to five-dimensional Coulomb phases and six-dimensional anomaly cancellation.
Can nongeometric phases enlarge the geometric F-theory classification? Discrete torsion can freeze smoothing moduli and alter gauge algebras, with frozen I*n fibers interpreted through O7+ planes.

How do local singular fibers and global data of elliptic fibrations encode the gauge sectors, matter and interactions of nonperturbative Type IIB compactifications with 7-branes, particularly through M-theory duality?

How do global structures of elliptic and genus-one fibrations encode continuous and discrete abelian gauge symmetries, global gauge groups, charge constraints and particle-physics constructions in F-theory?

Can other Higgsings, exceptional groups, singular parents or compactification frameworks yield larger primitive charges? Can these Weierstrass constructions support actual four-dimensional vacua after flux and superpotential conditions are imposed?
When does existence of some admissible SU(2) spectrum imply existence of a fundamental–adjoint spectrum?
Which anomaly and positivity data specify the low-energy theories compared with F-theory?
Which exotic representations and large abelian charges require special geometry or ingredients beyond conventional F-theory?
The F-theory setting supplies dynamical two-forms and electrically charged wrapped-D3 strings, allowing weak tensor coupling to be related to degeneration of the internal surface.

Which SU(2)×SU(3) Weierstrass fiber collisions admit smooth crepant resolutions, how are their resolutions connected, and what geometry and matter spectra govern the associated M-theory and F-theory compactifications?

How can six-dimensional F-theory spectra on freely acting, fibration-preserving quotients of elliptic Calabi–Yau threefolds be determined from the covering geometry and its symmetry action, including discrete gauge symmetries and strongly coupled sectors?
How can an F-theory base fill a periodic spin circle that cannot bound the ordinary spin hemisphere? The additional elliptic-fibration data change the allowed tangential structure.

Can double covers of rational elliptic threefolds systematically construct elliptically fibered Calabi–Yau threefolds with positive Mordell–Weil rank, yielding six-dimensional N=1 F-theory models with multiple U(1) factors?
Which Mordell-Weil torsion groups occur on smooth elliptically fibered Calabi-Yau varieties, and what restrictions follow for non-simply connected F-theory gauge groups and certain quotient torsors?

How can rational elliptic fourfolds and their double covers systematically generate four-dimensional N = 1 F-theory geometries with multiple section-derived U(1) factors, and can base geometry indicate compatible K3 fibrations and heterotic duals?

How can base-independent matter-locus classes and F-theory spectra be extracted efficiently from generic toric complete-intersection fibers, including fibers with multisections, and used to analyze Higgs chains ending in Z4 vacua?

Can an explicit parameterized Weierstrass construction realize the directly tuned Standard Model quotient gauge group with generic matter, and capture all allowed moduli for fixed gauge and divisor data?

How can projective duality classify maximal-rank singularities of rational elliptic 1/2 Calabi–Yau threefolds, expose their fibers and sections, and determine geometric inputs for six-dimensional N=1 F-theory on their double covers?

How can one classify ADE singularities of rational elliptic fourfold building blocks and their Calabi–Yau double covers, recover their defining hypersurfaces from a prescribed singularity type, and extract geometric gauge-sector information for 4D N = 1 F-theory?

Which compact elliptic Calabi-Yau fivefolds realize the largest known geometric field contents in 2d (0,2) F-theory, and how does gravitational anomaly cancellation constrain examples with smooth or singular fourfold bases?
How does a duality-twisted circle acquire a physical source when capped? In the F-theory description, a nontrivial torus automorphism around the circle becomes a singular elliptic fiber at the cap.

Can a higher-charge, non-UFD construction realize the fixed T=1 charge-one/charge-two spectrum while avoiding the enhancement seen in Morrison–Park form? Zero intersection of the two charge-three-supporting divisors is chosen to remove charge-three matter.

This resolved orientifold provides an explicit F-theory geometry in which wrapped-D3 string flows can be compared with KK towers. Movable and exceptional divisors permit both simple charge rays and more general rays whose volumes depend on the resolution chamber.
How do general P¹-bundles and degenerating P¹-fibrations enlarge F-theory base geometries, and how do base transitions, rational sections and fiber monodromy modify heterotic/F-theory duality?

Can the proposed diagnostic recover a nontrivial abelian charge spectrum directly from a singular Weierstrass construction? The example tunes Morrison–Park coefficients over a surface and supplies a generating section for this test.
How can infinite-distance complex-structure degenerations of elliptic K3 surfaces be classified through canonical Weierstrass models, and how does this geometry support their F-theory interpretation?

Which protected objects can constrain the gap of six-dimensional F-theory vacua? Wrapped D3 strings are accessible through the tensor sector even though KK modes, generic string excitations, and charged-particle masses are not reliably computable.

Construct a six-dimensional N=(1,0) F-theory model with Mordell–Weil torsion Z4⊕Z4, determine its gauge group and matter, and investigate its relation to charge completeness, stable degeneration and a heterotic dual.
How can divisor intersection numbers in resolved elliptic F-theory geometries be computed efficiently enough to access large-rank gauge groups?

Can flux breaking of widespread rigid exceptional gauge groups produce the Standard Model gauge group and net chiral spectrum with small generation numbers, without tuning the geometric gauge group through complex-structure moduli?
How can varying type-IIB axio-dilaton data and 7-branes be represented by the geometry of an elliptically fibered K3?

Does the universal tuned Standard Model gauge-group construction admit all three anomaly-free linear families of generic chiral matter through symmetry-preserving vertical flux, or does F-theory impose additional linear restrictions? What geometric restrictions affect their multiplicities?
Which BPS curve charges define EFT strings in a twisted rationally fibered F-theory base?

How large can charges of massless or light fields become under a U(1) in four-dimensional F-theory, particularly a U(1) decoupled from other gauge sectors? The paper constructs large-charge examples and asks whether their charges approach a landscape upper bound.

How can four-dimensional Type II orientifold and F-theory vacua realise the Standard Model gauge sector and chiral spectrum, and what further consistency and phenomenological conditions must such constructions satisfy?

How do genus-one Calabi–Yau threefolds with twisted affine fibers encode 5D M-theory spectra, their associated 6D F-theory Jacobians, rank-changing circle reductions, and transitions to untwisted geometries?

How can codimension-one non-minimal degenerations of elliptic Calabi–Yau threefolds be represented by resolved geometries suitable for extracting six-dimensional F-theory information at complex-structure infinite distance?

Classify the toric elliptic and genus-one fibrations in the Kreuzer–Skarke database, identify their fibers and bases modulo ambient-polytope automorphisms, and interpret ordinary and exotic examples through 6D F-theory.

Can flux breaking of rigid exceptional gauge groups produce Standard Model gauge symmetry, chirality and favorable phenomenology without extensive moduli tuning? How large can charges of light or massless U(1)-charged fields become in 4D F-theory?
How does F-theory on elliptically fibered K3 connect to a conventional orientifold and heterotic compactification, and how are departures from the constant-coupling locus corrected nonperturbatively?

What physical system realizes the four-dimensional N=2 gauge theories appearing in F-theory geometry, and how can its observables probe the exact axion–dilaton background, BPS masses and seven-brane instantons?

How do singularities of elliptic Calabi–Yau fibrations encode enhanced gauge symmetries and matter, including perturbative, non-perturbative and mixed heterotic enhancements, and their four-dimensional Coulomb branches?
Can an elliptically fibered Calabi–Yau (n+1)-fold admit a weak-coupling region formally described by a type IIB orientifold on an auxiliary complex n-fold, and when is that auxiliary space singular?
